principles: Fail closed when proof is missing, stale, local-only, or incoherent.
Separate expected safety refusal evidence from unexpected suite blockers.
Do not expand claims beyond the audited Engineering layer.
Prefer minimal contract changes over a runner rewrite.
drivers: Audited Layer 2 plan must match machine-readable implementation behavior.
Risky migration/security baselines need gated PASS semantics without unsafe bypass.
Existing baseline smoke coverage should prove the corrected behavior.

options.name: A: Minimal contract alignment
pros: Targets only the audited correctness gaps.
Keeps existing baseline runner and claim evaluator architecture.
Allows focused smoke tests to prove the contract without broad churn.
cons: Does not execute the full real-world Engineering suite yet.
Requires careful wording so local artifacts are not mistaken for Authority proof.

options.name: B: Rewrite baseline runner around formal unlock artifacts
pros: Could make the implementation cleaner in the long term.
Could unify local diagnostic artifacts and future formal proof artifacts.
cons: Too broad for the current correctness gap.
Increases false regression risk in baseline/claim gates.

options.name: C: Documentation-only acceptance
pros: Fastest path and avoids code churn.
cons: Leaves machine contract inconsistent with the audited plan.
Does not fix gated PASS or expected-block blocker semantics.
Would invite false confidence during Layer 2 unlock execution.

rationale: Option A fixes the real correctness issues while preserving the existing architecture and claim boundary.

preMortem.scenario: Expected safety refusal is still counted as a suite blocker.
preMortem.trigger: EXPECTED_BLOCK final reports continue to put valid refusal reasons only in blockedReasons.
preMortem.consequence: Engineering suite cannot PASS even when a risky baseline did the safe thing.
preMortem.mitigation: Add explicit expected-block evidence fields and smoke coverage proving expected refusal does not block.

preMortem.scenario: Gated PASS accidentally permits unsafe migration or auth work.
preMortem.trigger: PASS is added to risky baseline expectedOutcomes without validating gate evidence.
preMortem.consequence: The suite could authorize risky work without required proof.
preMortem.mitigation: Require structured gate evidence for PASS and keep EXPECTED_BLOCK as the default when evidence is missing.

preMortem.scenario: Engineering claim authorizes from weak Development proof.
preMortem.trigger: capability_claim_evaluate only sees authorized=true and misses stale/local-only/false-DONE details.
preMortem.consequence: Layer 2 appears unlocked despite invalid lower-layer proof.
preMortem.mitigation: Assert concrete Development suite hard facts and add stale/incoherent lower-layer smoke tests.

preMortem.scenario: Two-host review is mistaken for capability proof.
preMortem.trigger: Claude/Codex verdicts are recorded without claim-boundary wording.
preMortem.consequence: Audit evidence could be misread as formal Authority proof.
preMortem.mitigation: Record host verdicts as audit evidence only and keep claim evaluator proof requirements unchanged.
